findings.title: "SAME philosophy as player-accuracy.ts" is an imprecise framing
findings.problem: player-accuracy.ts sums per-stat absolute errors before dividing (to stop one stat's over-count cancelling another's under-count). The new metric sums each side's category volume first, then takes one |a-m|, which allows sub-stat cancellation within a group. This is intended (breakdown-agnostic volume) but the wording overstates equivalence.
findings.fix: Reword D2.1: it reuses the absolute-difference SHAPE applied to the per-category VOLUME total, not to summed per-stat errors, and deliberately does not guard against sub-stat cancellation.

findings.title: foulsDrawn is an undocumented member of the dropped-here set
findings.problem: bumpFootball classifies 'fouls drawn' into foulsDrawn, which no displayed category's parts include, so a foulsDrawn-only player is dropped. The divergence enumeration (ballRecoveries/groundDuels/aerials/headers) silently omits foulsDrawn, making the list read as exhaustive when it is not.
findings.fix: Add a parenthetical to FR5/D3 noting foulsDrawn also maps to no displayed category and is neither shown nor counted toward the drop rule.

findings.title: No AC exercises an over-count at the category level via the aggregator
findings.where: Acceptance Criteria (AC5/AC6 test the bare metric; AC7 is a clean tally)
findings.problem: The sub-stat-cancellation behaviour is only reachable through computePlayerCategoryTally's category summing; no AC pins it, so a future change to categoryTotal could pass all ACs while altering results.
findings.fix: Add AC7b: master ['Tackles Successful','Interceptions'] (Defensive m=2), analyst ['Blocks','Blocks','Clearances'] (Defensive a=3) => Defensive { a:3, m:2, pct:0.5 }.

findings.title: Scope chip uses teamDisplay while row labels keep canonical team
findings.where: D6 Team filter vs D6 Display-name note
findings.problem: The header scope chip maps canonical Home/Away to a club name via teamDisplay, but row labels show the raw canonical team for parity with the Player stats table. Both individually match existing sections, but the asymmetry is unstated and an implementer might unify them.
findings.fix: Add a line to D6 stating the asymmetry is deliberate (chip mirrors other section headers; row labels mirror the Player stats table) and must not be unified.
